title: The Latest in GPU, TPU, NIC and Other Device Support - WG Device Management
tldr: WG Device Management reviewed what Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) shipped in Kubernetes 1.37 and what is landing in 1.38, from device taints and extended-resource compatibility to partitionable devices and CPU allocation through DRA. Next up are DRA preemption, gang-aware preemption, richer hardware models and attaching GPUs to running pods.

key_points.text: Device plugins expose an opaque integer count; the working group formed after KubeCon EU 2024 because AI ASICs, RDMA NICs and CXL memory need richer modeling.
DRA has four parts: ResourceSlice to describe devices, ResourceClaim to request them (including under-specified asks like any GPU with 20 GB), the scheduler match, and the kubelet/driver setup.
ResourceSlice is aimed at vendors, ResourceClaim at users and DeviceClass at admins, who can inject policy without changing user manifests.
1.37: extended resource requests let admins move to DRA drivers while users keep asking for nvidia.com/gpu-style resources.
1.37: device taints mark a single failing accelerator instead of tainting the whole node and stranding healthy devices.
1.37 began DRA integration with workload-aware scheduling: resource claims attach to a pod group, plus faster scheduling of many DRA pods at once.

1.38: partitionable devices (main case NVIDIA MIG), consumable capacity (for example sharing NIC bandwidth), and binding conditions that wait for slow fabric-attached devices and can reschedule on failure.

Node allocatable resources via DRA (beta in 1.38) let CPU, memory and hugepages be allocated in a claim and aligned with the NIC and GPU, with the scheduler avoiding double counting against the container spec.
With workload-aware scheduling, a claim per pod-group replica can allocate a compute domain or TPU slice and clean it up when the replica scales down.
Adoption needs vendors to ship drivers and ecosystem projects to consume DRA; Karpenter, Cluster Autoscaler and KubeVirt are integrating.
The DRA plugin is a default kube-scheduler plugin; most new DRA features have a scheduling component.

numbers.text: DRA went GA in Kubernetes 1.34; since 1.36 two to three DRA features graduate to GA each release.
About 20 active features are tracked by the working group at any time.
Placing a NIC and GPU on the same PCIe root can give about 10x the IO performance between them.

open_gaps.text: DRA does not yet support preemption; an alpha is targeted for 1.38, and gang-level (workload-aware) preemption comes later.
Attaching and detaching GPUs on running pods (in-place mutability) is early, possibly alpha in 1.39.
Components that make their own scheduling decisions, like Kueue and autoscalers, must understand DRA's programmable scheduling; shared importable libraries are being built.
No public fractional TPU sharing yet.

opportunities.text: Follow the working group's live feature tracking sheet and weekly meetings (EU- and US-friendly times).
Use a DeviceClass with extended resources to move a cluster to a DRA driver without changing user manifests.
Help autoscalers and admission controllers support newer DRA features such as partitionable devices.
Try DRA for non-traditional resources, such as locally cached models or NVMe access, as discussed in Q&A.
